speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been having difficulty conceiving and experiencing discomfort during sexual activity; to help me identify the cause, have you noticed any specific pain, such as deep pelvic pain during intercourse or pain at the vaginal opening?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to vaginismus and possible male erectile dysfunction, with infertility likely due to unexplained factors or anatomical issues requiring further evaluation.
